assignment.description: A voice-based shopping list manager with smart suggestions.

sub_features.name: Voice Command Recognition
sub_features.detail: Allow users to add items to the shopping list using voice commands (e.g., 'Add milk', 'I need apples').

sub_features.name: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
sub_features.detail: Understand and process varied user phrases for flexibility (e.g., 'I want to buy bananas' vs. 'Add bananas to my list').

sub_features.name: Multilingual Support
sub_features.detail: Enable voice commands in multiple languages.

sub_features.name: Product Recommendations
sub_features.detail: Based on previous shopping history or preferences, suggest items the user is likely to need (e.g., 'It looks like you’re running low on bread').

sub_features.name: Seasonal Recommendations
sub_features.detail: Suggest items that are in season or on sale.

sub_features.name: Substitutes
sub_features.detail: Offer alternatives if a product is unavailable or if the user prefers a different option (e.g., suggest almond milk if the user mentions regular milk).

sub_features.name: Add / Remove / Modify Items
sub_features.detail: Allow users to add, remove, or modify items using voice commands (e.g., 'Remove milk from my list').

sub_features.name: Categorize Items
sub_features.detail: Automatically categorize items (e.g., dairy, produce, snacks) for better organization.

sub_features.name: Quantity Management
sub_features.detail: Specify quantities using voice (e.g., 'Add 2 bottles of water' or 'Buy 5 oranges').

sub_features.name: Item Search
sub_features.detail: Allow users to search for specific items by voice, including details like brand, size, or price range (e.g., 'Find me organic apples').

sub_features.name: Price Range Filtering
sub_features.detail: Voice-based filter to specify price ranges or brands (e.g., 'Find toothpaste under $5').

11_ui_ux.label: UI / UX (out of backend scope — noted for awareness)

sub_features.name: Minimalist Interface
sub_features.detail: Easy-to-use interface with a simple display of the shopping list.

sub_features.name: Visual Feedback
sub_features.detail: Display recognized items and actions in real time (e.g., show added items or confirmations).

sub_features.name: Mobile / Voice-Only Interface
sub_features.detail: Optimized for mobile devices and voice-only interactions.

12_hosting.label: Hosting (out of backend scope — noted for awareness)
12_hosting.detail: Deploy on a reliable platform (e.g., AWS, Firebase, Google Cloud) to manage voice recognition and interactions.

technical_freedom: Use any frameworks/technologies you're comfortable with
Free to use AI/ML services (any free tier)
Collect test data from public sources
deliverables: GitHub repository with source code and README
Brief write-up of your approach (200 words max)

rules: Repository size should be within GitHub limits and fully downloadable
Must be publicly accessible / not protected
File size should not exceed Google Drive limits (ideally < 1GB)

include: Basic application with all required assignment and project code files

dependency_policy: No extra modules or package files should be added
Use only what is strictly required for the assignment/project
Keep dependencies minimal and native whenever possible
pre_submission_checklist: Ensure the app runs without errors
Code files are properly structured and named
Branch name is set to main
Repository or Google Drive link is publicly accessible and downloadable
Submission size is within GitHub / Google Drive limits
Proper documentation or comments where necessary

plan_alignment_notes.backend_scope: Points 1, 2, 3, 4 are fully in backend scope. Points 11 (UI/UX) and 12 (Hosting) are noted for awareness but are out of scope for the current backend build.

compliance_flags.no_env_in_repo: The .env file must NOT be committed — must be in .gitignore.
compliance_flags.no_venv_in_repo: The venv/ folder must NOT be committed — must be in .gitignore.
compliance_flags.no_pycache: __pycache__/ and *.pyc files must NOT be committed.
compliance_flags.minimal_dependencies: requirements.txt must list ONLY the packages strictly needed.
compliance_flags.gitignore_required: A proper .gitignore covering the above is mandatory.
